As a Data Scientist on the Mapping team, you will collaborate with our world class team of scientists, engineers, product managers, and designers to grow and improve the quality of recommended routes and accuracy of our travel time estimations. We're looking for a passionate, driven Data Scientist who is excited to dive into our geospatial, behavioural and mobility data, and build a best-in-class mapping product that provides safe, efficient, and seamless navigation for our rideshare drivers.
 Data Science is at the heart of Lyft’s products and decision-making. You will leverage data and rigorous, analytical thinking to shape our mapping products and make business decisions that put our customers first. The Mapping team serves models and systems that determine the most efficient routes, fastest travel estimates and process real-time map data signals to detect traffic, closures and slowdowns. Working with our business and analytics partners, the team owns tools to ensure Lyft offers routes that our users trust. This will involve identifying and scoping opportunities, recommending technical solutions, designing experiments, and measuring the impact of new features. You will help us solve some of the most impactful problems in Mapping, including:
 How do we accurately predict acute and chronic traffic conditions?
 How do we improve the recommendations of our routing algorithms?
 How do we keep our travel estimation promises to our riders and drivers?
 How do we benchmark and measure the success of our services?
 Responsibilities:
 Own the complete lifecycle of algorithmic solutions from problem formulation, data exploration, and feature engineering to deployment, monitoring, and iteration
 Prioritize and lead deep dives into our data to uncover new product and business opportunities
 Partner closely with Engineering to build and scale production-grade ML systems, real-time inference services, batch pipelines, and feature stores
 Design, implement, and analyze different types of experiments, and facilitate and foster data-driven and informed decision making and prioritization
 Drive scientific excellence by introducing modern techniques in ML, optimization, reinforcement learning, or graph-based methods to unlock new product capabilities
 Establish metrics that measure the health of our products, as well as rider and driver experience
 Translate complex business challenges into concrete algorithmic solutions in close collaboration with Product, Engineering, Operations, and Science teams
 Experience:
 Advanced degree in a quantitative field such as statistics, physics, economics, operations research, neuroscience, or engineering, or relevant work experience
 3+ years hands-on experience in a data science or machine learning role working with production machine learning models and optimization systems
 Passion for solving unstructured and non-standard mathematical problems
 Experience independently driving multi-project algorithmic scopes and navigating technical ambiguity from ideation to delivery
 Experience with machine learning models in production, making practical tradeoffs among algorithm sophistication, compute complexity, maintainability, and extensibility in production environments
 Strong oral and written communication skills, and ability to collaborate with and influence cross-functional partners 
 Working knowledge of modern machine learning frameworks and distributed computing systems, including PyTorch, TensorFlow, Ray, Spark, etc.
 Benefits: 
 Mental health benefits
 Family building benefits
 Child care and pet benefits
 Subsidized commuter benefits and Lyft ride credits

Job Title: Power System Engineering Technologist (P.L. Eng.)
 Job Level: ENG C
 Date Posted: September 8, 2026
 Closing Date: Open until the positions is filled
 Job Type: Full-time Permanent
 Category: Internal/External Opportunities 
 Location: Calgary
 Powering a bright future starts with you! 
 Oh, and, what do we do? 
 We power Alberta! Our transmission lines deliver electricity to millions of Albertans 24 hours a day, seven days a week. When you’re on our team, you’re supporting Alberta’s homes, farms, businesses and industries by providing the safe, reliable and affordable electricity they rely on. Whether working in the field or in the office, every AltaLinker contributes to keeping the lights on. Want to join our team? We’re excited to share that we are hiring a Power System Engineering Technologist (P.L.Eng.) on AltaLink’s Project Engineering team.
 Job Description: 
 AltaLink is seeking a Power System Engineering Technologist (P.L. Eng.) to join the Project Engineering team. The successful candidate will focus on development, validation, and management of transmission-system and electrical-equipment models. They will work with internal teams, the AESO, and other stakeholders, to prepare transmission modelling data packages (PDUPs), line-impedance calculations, and facility-rating reports; support small interconnection studies; provide system-capacity, power-flow, and short-circuit information; and help improve modelling processes and procedures. The role is also responsible for ensuring modelling data records, documentation, and submissions comply with applicable AESO ISO Rules, Alberta Reliability Standards, and associated requirements. 
 This opportunity is open to individuals who are registered with the Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta (APEGA) as a Professional Licensee (Engineering), P.L. (Eng.), or individuals who are eligible to obtain that designation. The successful candidate will apply sound technical judgement, maintain accurate and auditable modelling records, and contribute to the safe, reliable, and economic interconnection to and operation of Alberta’s transmission system.
 Responsibilities: 
 Under the supervision of the Manager, Project Engineering, this individual will be accountable for all or in part of the following: 
 Development, authentication, and submission of complete, accurate, and timely transmission modelling data packages to the AESO for existing facilities and planned additions, modifications, and re-ratings of electrical facilities and infrastructure in accordance with AESO modelling-data requirements.
 Validation and maintenance of existing transmission-system and electrical-equipment models to ensure they accurately represent current facility configurations, equipment characteristics, operating conditions, and approved system changes.
 Development and maintenance of line-impedance calculations and reports.
 Development and maintenance of facility-rating reports for existing and planned transmission facilities.
 Ensuring modelling data, models, supporting documentation, and submissions comply with applicable AESO ISO Rules, Alberta Reliability Standards, and AltaLink Standards.
 Supporting the delivery of facility studies for system and customer projects, by providing transmission modelling, current and future system capacity assessments, power flow analysis, and short circuit information to other internal teams and external customers.
 Collaborating with AESO teams to improve modelling processes and procedures.
 Qualifications: 
 Electrical Engineering Technology Diploma. A focus on power systems is considered an asset.
 Professional Licensee (Engineering) P.L. Eng designation with the Association of Professional Engineers & Geoscientists of Alberta (APEGA) or eligible to obtain such designation, with a defined scope of practice applicable to the duties of the position.
 Minimum of six 6 years of relevant experience related to engineering or modeling of high voltage transmission or distributions systems. Preference will be given to candidates with two or more years of specific engineering experience related to the modeling of electrical transmission and/or distribution systems and to candidates with a working knowledge of AESO rules and requirements. 
 Technical knowledge and understanding of transmission system modeling operation and planning.
 Documented experience with PTI’s (Power Technology Incorporated) PSSE program and other power system analysis tools such as PSCAD/EMTDC is an asset.
 Familiar with the AESO Modeling Data requirements and rules.
 Strong verbal and written (reporting, graphical) communication skills with ability to work in a team environment and positively influence others.
 Effective communication and interpersonal skills to interface with team members and customers to promote positive customer outcomes.
 Excellent organizational skills and ability to manage a wide variety of issues on multiple projects simultaneously.  
 Working knowledge of Microsoft Office: Word, Power Point, Excel etc.

Private markets are one of the largest, most complex, and most underserved corners of global finance. Our mission at Juniper Square is to unlock their full potential. With $300B+ under administration and 700,000+ LPs on platform, we’ve built the scale to match our ambition. And with JunieAI, our purpose-built AI platform, we’re reimagining how private markets operate, embedding intelligence across every workflow. Founder-led since 2014, backed by $350M+ in funding, and now 1,000+ employees strong, we’re building a company designed to shape the future of private markets for decades to come.

ABOUT YOUR ROLE

As the Senior Compensation & Equity Manager, you’ll own compensation and equity programs end-to-end for a global, distributed workforce, serving as the analytical engine of our Total Rewards function. Reporting to the VP of Total Rewards & People Operations, you’ll partner with Finance, FP&A, Talent Acquisition, and People Business Partners to keep our pay programs market-competitive, internally equitable, and built to scale. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role for someone with deep compensation and equity experience who can add value from day one — owning market pricing, the annual rewards cycle, bonus programs, and equity strategy while giving recruiters and leaders clear, data-backed recommendations. Our Senior Benefits & People Programs Manager serves as your backup on compensation and equity operations.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own market pricing and band builds across levels, job families, and geographies (U.S., Canada, India, UK), maintaining the Jobs Table as the source of truth and keeping systems in sync.

 - Lead the annual band refresh, including cost modeling for level and band changes, and review internal pay relativities, job architecture, leveling, and titling decisions.

 - Serve as the first point of contact for comp band, level, and offer recommendations for recruiters and People Business Partners, backed by compa-ratio and internal equity analysis, and advise leaders on promotions, off-cycle adjustments, relocations, and retention packages.

 - Price executive and hard-to-benchmark roles with external advisors where proprietary data is needed, and partner with RevOps and Finance on quota-carrying compensation plans.

 - Run the annual rewards cycle in Pave end to end, modeling budgets by country and reporting cycle outcomes to People leadership.

 - Own the Company Performance Plan and other bonus programs end to end.

 - Administer one-time, spot, retention, and milestone bonuses, including approval workflows and award letters, and partner with the VP of Total Rewards & People Operations and Finance on bonus plan design, including for acquired teams and international populations.

 - Partner with the VP of Total Rewards & People Operations on equity strategy and model equity budgets and Board proposals.

 - Benchmark equity for new hire, promotion, and executive grants, and advise on equity treatment for international moves, new countries, and acquisitions.

 - Own the quarterly grant cycles submitted for Board approval, reconcile equity data across Shareworks, HiBob, and Pave, and lead employee equity education.

 - Use structured candidate compensation data from Ashby to track where we win and lose on pay and flag when a band needs to be revisited, and support pay equity reviews to keep posted pay ranges current.

 - Identify opportunities to automate high-repetition compensation and equity workflows, partnering with the team to embed AI-powered tooling that reduces manual lift without sacrificing accuracy.
   
   
   

QUALIFICATIONS

 - 7+ years of compensation experience, ideally within a SaaS or technology company operating across multiple geographies.

 - Deep expertise in market pricing, job matching, and band construction using compensation survey data; Radford experience is strongly preferred.

 - Hands-on experience with equity strategy and operations, including grant guidelines, Board approval cycles, and equity administration platforms such as Shareworks.

 - Experience administering bonus and variable pay plans and running compensation cycles in a platform such as Pave, with advanced spreadsheet and HRIS data modeling skills.

 - Ability to turn analysis into a clear recommendation for leaders, hold a position with data, and exercise sound judgment with highly confidential data.

 - Exposure to international compensation (Canada, India, UK) or sales compensation design, a CCP/CEP certification, or hands-on experience with AI-powered tools such as Claude, is a plus.

 - Exceptional relationship-building skills and the ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment with shifting priorities.

COMPENSATION

Compensation for this position includes a base salary, equity, and a variety of benefits. As a member of Waabi's Operations organization, the Senior Data Analyst will own and evolve the metrics, dashboards, and analytical foundations used to understand and operate the fleet. This role is critical to ensuring our operational data is accurate, consistent, and actionable across fleet performance, utilization, uptime, operational readiness, and commercial reporting. We need someone who will take initiative, live and breathe the data, and come forward with ideas on what metrics to explore, what patterns matter, and where operational performance can improve. This role is not just about reporting on the business, it is about helping shape how the business operates through data-backed insight.
 
You will…
Define, implement, track, manage, and continuously improve core operational metrics used to measure fleet performance, efficiency, utilization, uptime, and readiness.
Build and maintain data pipelines, analytical datasets, data models, and automated workflows that consolidate operational data from multiple sources, validate their completeness and integrity, partnering with Data Platform on upstream pipelines and infrastructure.
Build, maintain, and standardize dashboards and recurring reporting across operations to ensure accuracy, consistency, and alignment with business needs, converting manual tracking and fragmented reporting into automated workflows.
Analyze productivity, delays, downtime, and other operational inefficiencies to identify trends, root causes, and improvement opportunities.
Proactively propose new metrics, dashboards, and analyses based on what the data is showing, not only on predefined requests.
Quantify the impact of operational issues, including lost hours, miles, missions, and other business-critical outputs.
Build structured tracking across the mission lifecycle, including pre-mission, in-mission, and post-mission performance.
Support internal and external reporting for commercial operations and demos, including metrics such as completion rates, cancellations, and execution quality.
Identify data gaps, quality issues, and inconsistencies across systems, and recommend scalable improvements.
Partner closely with Ops, Commercial, Data Platform, and other stakeholders to clarify requirements and deliver actionable insight.
Help convert manual tracking and fragmented reporting into reliable, scalable datasets and automated reporting workflows.
Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in Data, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
3-5 years of experience in a dedicated data analyst, analytics, or business intelligence role.
Strong SQL skills and experience working with relational datasets, plus experience with Python or R for analysis, pandas preferred.
Familiarity with dbt (data build tool) and modern analytics workflows for modeling and transforming data.
Experience cleaning, validating, reconciling, and analyzing data from multiple sources.
Experience building dashboards and recurring reports using BI tools, with the ability to quickly adopt new analytics and AI-assisted tools and workflows.
Strong statistical literacy, with demonstrated ability to apply methods like significance testing, regression analysis, and distribution analysis in order to identify the true drivers of performance.
Strong problem-solving skills, sound business judgment, and the ability to independently turn ambiguous questions into structured analysis, surface insights, and make recommendations.
Strong communication skills and the ability to translate data into clear takeaways for operational and leadership audiences.
Bonus:
Experience working with operations, logistics, fleet, transportation, or other operationally complex datasets, including customer-facing or commercial reporting.
Experience with modern analytics and operational tooling, including cloud data warehouses, ETL or API-based ingestion, workflow automation, operational systems, and evaluation or adoption of new analytical or AI-assisted tools.

You own architectural design and its automation for our data center and industrial projects — from building layouts and equipment access to envelopes, life safety, and construction documentation.
 You'll deliver real architectural packages on live projects while building the parametric engine that generates them for every future site. You'll build alongside our existing structural and architectural automation efforts, connecting building design with the engineering systems inside it.
 This isn't a visualization role. You're designing buildings that get constructed — and building the software that makes the process repeatable.
 You don't need a software background. You need to understand buildings, think in systems, and use AI to turn your design knowledge into working tools.
 What you’ll achieve 
 Deliver architectural packages for live projects: space planning, floor plans, elevations, sections, envelope assemblies, architectural details, schedules, and coordinated construction documentation.
 Build a parametric architectural design engine that turns project requirements, equipment layouts, site constraints, and building-system requirements into coordinated models and drawings.
 Automate the repetitive work: layout iterations, room and door schedules, drawing production, and checks for equipment clearances, circulation, accessibility, and egress — with clear review points for decisions that require professional judgment.
 Connect architecture with civil, structural, mechanical, and electrical design. When equipment, capacity, or structural grids change, the building layout and documentation should update with them — not require days of manual redrawing.
 Use AI coding agents to ship these workflows. Turn decisions made on one project into reusable rules, components, and tools for the next.
 You must 
 Understand how buildings work — space planning, circulation, building envelopes, constructability, and the interfaces between architecture and engineering.
 Have taken designs beyond a concept: through detailed modeling, construction documentation, fabrication, or construction. Show us what you personally contributed.
 Think parametrically. Understand which design decisions can become repeatable rules, which depend on project-specific constraints, and which require human judgment.
 Be able to ship working tools with AI coding agents today, even without a traditional software background.
 Take responsibility for design quality. Research and apply relevant requirements, verify automated outputs, and resolve coordination issues rather than passing them downstream.
 You do not need to 
 Have prior data center or industrial-project experience.
 Have a CS degree or identify as a software engineer.
 Have spent your career at a conventional architecture firm.

Then this role may be for you! We’re looking for a Success Enablement Manager to be part of our Success Enablement team.

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. The Team:

The Enablement team is a central function within Jobber’s Customer Success organization, supporting the growth and performance of Product Support and Customer Onboarding. As a Center of Excellence, Enablement owns the programs, playbooks, tools, and measurement frameworks that drive operational excellence and skill development across these teams. We work cross-functionally to ensure that every team member, regardless of channel or customer type, has the knowledge, confidence, and support to deliver value. That value is measured in outcomes: customers who activate faster, stay longer, and get more out of the product.

The Role:

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Success Enablement, the Success Enablement Manager will give our Product Support and Customer Onboarding teams the information, content, and tools they need to operate more effectively.

You will own enablement end to end for both teams. That means building how specialists ramp, how they stay current as the product changes, how they access the right answer in the moment, and how they keep improving once they are proficient. It also means raising the ceiling on what those conversations deliver. An onboarding session that activates a business on the features it actually needs, and a high-quality support interaction that also surfaces a product or feature the customer is missing, are both revenue moments. Service quality comes first in both. A specialist who has not solved the problem in front of them has not earned the next conversation. Your job is to make that judgement teachable, repeatable, and measurable.

You will build the needs discovery and product positioning frameworks specialists use live, enable the Next Best Action recommendations that surface in their workspace, and partner closely with our frontline manager group to help them hit their KPIs across service levels, quality, activation, adoption, and retention.

The Success Enablement Manager will:

 - Own the enablement lifecycle for Product Support and Customer Onboarding, from new hire ramp and certification through continuous development for tenured specialists.

 - Build and maintain the needs discovery and positioning frameworks specialists use in live customer conversations, so the right product reaches the right customer at the right moment.

 - Create and maintain Jobber’s Support and Onboarding playbooks, including activation paths by plan and industry, adoption plays for underused features, objection handling, and retention conversations, and ensure consistency of process and messaging across channels.

 - Enable Next Best Action adoption. Train specialists to read the recommendation, confirm the customer need behind it, and act on it inside their existing workflow.

 - Design, build and test in-person, virtual and on-demand enablement content, and partner with Knowledge Management so the same guidance is available in the flow of work.

 - Partner with our QA function to turn quality trends into targeted coaching and training, closing the loop between what we measure and what we teach.

 - Work with Product Marketing, Success Operations and Analytics to identify process and content gaps, and develop the resources (customer stories, competitive intelligence, collateral) that help specialists move conversations forward.

 - Connect enablement to outcomes. Tie program delivery to activation, feature adoption, retention, CSAT, and qualified opportunities, and report on what is working and what is not.

 - Contribute to, help organize and champion important team moments like quarterly kickoffs, lunch and learns, and certification pushes.

To be successful, you should have:

 - Demonstrated experience in customer success, customer service, onboarding, or sales within a high volume, short cycle, B2B SaaS environment, with a track record of consistent achievement of targets and motivating others to do the same.

 - Demonstrated previous experience in revenue driven roles which had targets, such as in Sales or Retention.

 - Experience building out and executing playbooks and training programs that improve both service quality and commercial outcomes.

 - Strong project management knowledge, including creating workback plans to drive projects from conception to the finish line.

 - A strong grasp of activation and adoption. You understand what gets a customer to first value, what keeps them using a product, and how to design enablement that moves both.

 - Working knowledge of needs-based conversations. You can teach a specialist to uncover a customer problem, connect it to the right product or feature, and position the value in plain language.

 - Comfort with standard SaaS retention and expansion metrics such as NRR, GRR, churn, save rate, expansion MRR, and attach and adoption rates. You can read a dashboard, find the gap, and build the program that closes it.

 - Exposure to Next Best Action or recommendation technology (Salesforce or similar), or a clear appetite to learn it. You will help shape how recommendations are framed, trained, and adopted on the floor.

 - The ability to dig into a project. You’ll need a strong understanding of how our team operates, what drives success and what resonates with our customers. Seeing the solution from different angles and providing solutions that cater to different learning styles.

 - A knack for identifying gaps in our process and how to fill them. Thinking beyond our current process and coming up with smart solutions.

 - A high level of organizational and time management skills.

 - The ability to collaborate with business partners across the organization. Working with specialists, Product Marketing and other leadership members, you’ll be required to articulate strategic ideas, learn the inner workings of Jobber, and then deliver on high-level concepts.

 - The ability to teach yourself, and others. Our team uses a variety of tools, so you’ll need to learn the most efficient uses of them and then spread that knowledge amongst the team.

Hi 👋🏾, I’m Abhik https://www.linkedin.com/in/abhikpramanik/, Ashby’s Co-Founder and CTO. Ashby is growing fast, which means exponential growth across every product metric: jobs, applications, interviews, you name it. We’re not slowing down, and as a result, keeping Ashby performant and reliable is a company priority. We need your leadership to do that now and in the future.

We’ve already assembled a fantastic Platform & Infrastructure team of 11 engineers (all Senior+, >70% Staff), and they’ve done an excellent job handling our growth, but the management and leadership of Platform & Infrastructure have been diffused across our Engineering leaders. As we hit our next level of scale, it’s time for us to hire an Engineering leader responsible for performance and reliability, and for building out the team that ensures those. Hopefully, that’s you!

 


THE ROLE

In this role, you will report directly to me, and your responsibilities will include:

 - Building and maintaining a long-term vision and 6-month roadmap for Platform & Infrastructure.

 - Growing the Platform & Infrastructure team. You’ll hire ICs, managers, and build out a headcount plan. This will include determining if more specialized roles need to be established (e.g., DB Admin).

 - Building and maintaining an excellent relationship with Product Engineering. The ideal state is that Product Engineering can move incredibly fast independently without breaking performance or reliability, and Platform & Infrastructure doesn’t feel like they’re always cleaning up someone else’s “mess.” Today, there’s a great relationship, but there’s always room for improvement!

 - Assessing and improving our monitoring and incident management process. Again, we’re doing relatively well here, but there’s always room to improve. For example, making uptime measurement easier and improving coordination with Support during incidents.

 - Maintaining vendor relationships and negotiating pricing for our critical hosting and observability infrastructure, including AWS, ClickHouse, Datadog, and Braintrust. They have a meaningful impact on gross margin and need to be kept in check.

 - You’ve managed managers. Managing other leaders is a very different ball game, and not everyone enjoys it or thrives in it. Within your first 6 months, you’ll most likely have to hire a manager underneath you.

 - If you have experience managing developer experience and developer tools, building out a dedicated team for DevEx. If you don’t have experience here, DevEx will report into Product Engineering. Happy to discuss once we meet!

A big part of our secret sauce is how we run Engineering. We achieve incredible speed and quality by discarding many industry norms and being optimistic about Engineers. We consider what makes exceptional Engineers exceptional, then figure out how to hire them and build an environment that gives them the freedom and agency to be exceptional. You’ll be a key leader in ensuring that continues!

 


THE QUALIFICATIONS

We’re entrusting you with a company priority, so we want you to know how to scale products and build the great teams that do that. This means:

 - You played an important role leading a company through a high-growth period (either as an IC Lead or Engineering Leader). You had to make high-quality decisions under pressure. That often meant striking a balance between short-term fixes to keep the product from falling over and long-term investments to ensure it didn’t happen again.

 - You have experience hiring and building hiring processes, and enjoy it! You’ve designed interviews, interview loops, and led hiring strategy.

 - You have a track record of excellent collaboration with other departments. You were a key contributor to company-level initiatives that involved Product Engineering, Product, Sales, or Support. Those departments felt heard and supported, yet positively challenged by you.

 - You have a background in writing production software (far beyond scripts). Our Platform & Infrastructure team is exclusively made up of strong software engineers, not just folks who scale the systems software runs on. They can jump into any part of our app, understand the code, and modify the underlying logic. We expect you to have similar experience to grow and upskill the team.

 - You are knowledgeable about platform and infrastructure technologies, networking, and hardware. You know how Kubernetes goes beyond a Container Orchestration Platform, how traffic flows between Load Balancers and Pods, and how the intricacies of the underlying hardware can cause Cloud abstractions to break, etc.

 - You are a great communicator, particularly in writing. You’ll need to be able to go deep with Infrastructure Engineers in conversations while also communicating those concepts to folks like myself who have much less experience.

You should be comfortable managing a team spanning from the Americas West Coast to Europe. You’ll be able to hire managers to focus on specific time zones, but I expect you to have skips with some engineers (and you should want to, too!). To ensure a reasonable work schedule, we’re only hiring candidates who live in the PST-GMT time zone.

 


WHAT WE’RE BUILDING

As engineers, we are used to tooling that makes us better at what we do. When we started Ashby, we saw the opposite with Talent Acquisition software. Recruiting teams were leveling up how they did their work, but instead of software meeting this new standard, it held them back.

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example. Recruiting teams wanted to schedule candidates faster, track interviewer preparation and quality, and do it with half the headcount. A recruiter needed to manually collect availability from the candidate, identify qualified interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and make any last-minute adjustments as availability changed. They must do this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 🥵 TA software didn’t help.

As hiring managers, we know TA is a critical function, and as engineers, we know software can do better. So, we built and continue to build Ashby to give TA teams the highest standard of tooling. Software that’s intelligent and powerful. Software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We want other functions and departments to be jealous of what TA teams can do with Ashby, and today they often are!

 


WHY YOU SHOULDN’T APPLY

 - You’ve always been a line manager or never led a department within Engineering. You haven’t led the definition and evolution of culture and processes.

 - You don’t enjoy coding or don’t find time to stay up-to-date on technology. We believe great leaders are folks who were great engineers themselves. That starts with loving the craft and never giving it up.

 - You went into management because it was the only growth path available. We want folks who could have been Principal engineers (or were one!).

 - You're happy with a team of engineers who are predominantly early-career or mid-career or don't thrive with ownership or autonomy. You believe that with enough guardrails, the team can get things done.

 - To you, a Staff or Principal Engineer is someone who spends most of their time project managing or conducting architecture reviews. You don’t believe staff and principal engineers could lead by the example they set or the leverage they create through their work.

 - You’re not optimistic or convinced that we can build a large engineering team that functions differently from the status quo. You think, at some size, common processes need to be implemented to ensure consistent delivery (e.g., sprint planning, product managers writing in-depth specifications). You might not say it out loud, but you think, at some size, compromises have to be made for the sake of hiring numbers or consistency.

 


ENGINEERING CULTURE

Our engineering culture is motivated by Benji’s (Co-founder and CEO) and my belief that a small, talented team, given the right environment, can build high-quality software fast (and work regular hours!). We do it through:

 - Minimal process with ownership over decisions normally made by product and design

 - Natural collaboration and deliberate communication

 - Investing in tools and abstractions that give us leverage, including LLM-driven dev tooling.

 - Putting effort into building a diverse team

 


MINIMAL PROCESS & LOTS OF OWNERSHIP

The best engineers we’ve worked with delivered reliably magical outcomes. They often discovered problems, prioritized the right ones, and relentlessly drove them to solutions that were not only successful but often brilliant and creative. While they did this with minimal oversight, stakeholders were never in the dark as to what was going on, and no setback was a surprise.

Traditional development processes aren’t meant for the best engineers. Their purpose is to create consistent outcomes regardless of the engineer’s skill. But consistency comes at the expense of an engineer’s time and freedom—both ingredients necessary to generate those magical outcomes. As a result, process stifles the best engineers and doesn’t give others the opportunity to practice the behaviors that made the best engineers the “best.”

At Ashby, we want to build an environment that encourages every engineer to be their best. So, every Engineer runs their project. Product Managers (and Designers) build strategy, do customer research, and hand off problem briefs to Engineers. Engineers take on the rest: they research the problem, write product specs, build wireframes, and implement their solution end-to-end. We rely on engineers, not process, to push information outward to the relevant folks (e.g., Product Managers) and pull folks in to help (e.g., Designers, Infra). It’s a new level of ownership for many engineers, but we’d rather an engineer fail a bit and coach up their skills than use process as a crutch. Not everyone succeeds in our culture, but those who do thrive.

 


COLLABORATION IS NATURAL & COMMUNICATION IS DELIBERATE

Our engineering team consists of lifelong learners who are talented but also humble and kind (meet them here https://www.ashbyhq.com/team!). These attributes create an environment where collaboration happens naturally. We combine this with research, prototyping, and written proposals to see around corners and get feedback from the team across time zones. Focus time is something that we hold sacred, and, with thoughtful and deliberate communication, engineers are in <2h meetings per week (I wrote about it here https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/company/thoughtful-communication).

Who we are
 About Stripe
 About the team
 The Stripe Marketing organization is undergoing a fundamental transformation in how it works. We're building a team of Forward Deployed AI Accelerators (FDAs) embedded directly with marketing cohorts to make AI the default mode for all work — not an occasional tool, but the foundation of how every marketer at Stripe executes.
 Today, marketers are already achieving remarkable results — building their own data dashboards, creating agents that compress multi-day processes, and authoring tools that accelerate workflows. The FDA team exists to take what's working and systematically scale it across the entire marketing organization.
 What you'll do
 As a Forward Deployed AI Accelerator for Sales Development, you'll be embedded with the Sales Development (SD) team. You'll work directly with SD reps, managers, and leadership to understand how the team works, and you'll build the AI tools and automations that make that work faster and better. Your measure of success is the improvement in the speed and quality of the SD team’s work that your builds drive.
 Responsibilities
 Identify the highest-leverage workflows in SD's day-to-day work by deeply understanding the processes, inputs, and outputs behind them
 Build custom tools, agents, automations, and skills tailored to how SD works
 Work with SD leaders to prioritize what to build, and be clear about what is and isn't worth building
 Ship quickly, put working versions in front of users, and improve them based on how the team uses them
 Make what you build reliable: understandable, documented, and maintainable as data, systems, and processes change
 Measure the effect of what you ship, using before-and-after evidence on time saved, quality, or work made possible
 Partner with engineering, analytics, and operations teams when a tool needs production systems, sensitive data, or long-term ownership
 Share results with SD leadership and the wider FDA team
 Who you are
 We're looking for people who have already used AI to change how real work gets done.
 You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You've built things that other people used, or that ran in production systems, and that measurably improved the speed or quality of their work.
 You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new work becomes viable. 
 You learn the work quickly. You may have direct experience in sales development, sales operations, or marketing, or you quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of a new team. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it.
 You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions.
 You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders.
 You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next week.

BUILD SOMETHING PEOPLE LOVE

Wealthsimple is Canada’s leading financial innovator. The company offers a full suite of simple, sophisticated financial products across managed investing, do-it-yourself trading, cryptocurrency, tax filing, spending and saving. Wealthsimple currently serves more than 4 million Canadians and holds over $169 billion in assets under administration. The company was founded in 2014 by a team of financial experts and technology entrepreneurs, and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada.

About the team

We build the products and infrastructure that millions of Canadians trust with their financial lives. Data & Engineering at Wealthsimple spans everything from the client-facing apps to the systems running underneath them — and we hold ourselves to a high bar on both. We move fast, but we build thoughtfully: quality, security, and scalability aren’t trade-offs here, they’re the standard.

The Production Engineering team sits within Platform Experience, on the boundary between Platform and Product. Our mandate is to raise reliability across Wealthsimple’s most critical flows — reducing incidents, helping service teams ship safely, and turning individual fixes into platform-wide improvements. We measure ourselves against two targets: 99.9% uptime on critical flows, and fewer than 1% of weekly active users experiencing errors in the app. If you want to work on hard problems with people who care deeply about craft, you’ll fit right in.

 

About the role

This is a new role — one that doesn’t yet exist at Wealthsimple — and it’s a meaningful one. As a Staff Software Developer on Production Engineering, you’ll bring senior technical leadership to the work of making Wealthsimple more reliable at scale. You’ll work across platform and product teams, identify the highest-leverage reliability problems, and build solutions that don’t just fix the immediate issue but raise the floor for everyone. This isn’t a role where you sit in one corner of the codebase. It’s a role where you shape how engineering gets done across the company.

 

What you’ll do

 - Improve the platform to prevent incidents — designing and driving adoption of guardrails, sensible defaults, and engineering standards that reduce the likelihood of failures across services

 - Build tooling that reduces time to mitigation when incidents occur, including contributing to our in-house product on AI-assisted incident response

 - Own the investigation and follow-through on load test findings — translating results into concrete reliability improvements across critical flows

 - Work across platform and product engineering teams as a technical influencer — participating in architecture and readiness reviews, coaching service owners, and driving adoption of scalable reliability practices

 - Identify recurring failure patterns and design platform-level fixes that prevent them from showing up again in a different service

 - Contribute to the team’s reliability syncs with product engineering, helping align on incident themes, critical-flow risks, and the next highest-leverage initiatives

 

Skills you bring

 - 8+ years of software engineering experience, with significant time in platform, infrastructure, or SRE work

 - Demonstrated track record of improving reliability at scale — reducing incidents, building guardrails, or driving operational standards across multiple teams

 - Strong proficiency in backend systems and distributed architecture; you can diagnose complex failure modes across a service mesh

 - Experience with load testing and capacity planning, and the ability to translate findings into concrete engineering improvements

 - Proven ability to work across engineering teams as a technical influencer — driving adoption of standards and practices without direct authority

 - Familiarity with Kubernetes, Helm, Argo and modern deployment tooling

 - Strong written and verbal communication — comfortable presenting findings and recommendations to both engineering teams and senior leadership

 

Who you are

 - You think in systems — you’re not looking for the fix, you’re looking for what caused the problem and how to make sure it doesn’t happen elsewhere

 - You’re comfortable working without direct authority; you build credibility through the quality of your thinking and the clarity of your recommendations

 - You hold a high bar for operational excellence without making it someone else’s problem to catch up to — you bring people along

 - You’re energised by ambiguity, not slowed down by it; you know how to prioritise when everything feels urgent

 - You’re curious about where AI-assisted tooling is headed in reliability engineering, and you want to help shape how we use it — not just observe it from a distance

 About Fulfillment IQ
 Fulfillment IQ (FIQ) is a supply chain engineering and transformation company that helps brands, retailers, and 3PLs design, build, and scale high-performance logistics operations.

Our teams combine deep domain expertise with strong technical capability, delivering outcomes through consulting, systems implementation, and proprietary platforms that accelerate time-to-value and reduce delivery risk. 
 If you enjoy working in complex environments, partnering closely with clients and experts, and seeing your work make a tangible impact on how global commerce moves, this is a place where your skills and judgment come to life. 
 Marketing at FIQ 
 We are building a small, hands-on marketing team with one job: turn conferences and useful content into qualified conversations with the right buyers at brands, retailers and 3PLs. The team runs two motions: 
 Conference and buyer events: we attend a conference because the right buyers are there and a practice has a relevant offer, and we add dinners, roundtables or expert sessions when that improves access to those buyers. 
 Named-account campaigns: we pick accounts with our sellers, identify the buyer and a credible business problem, and reach them through content, organic LinkedIn, email, the website and coordinated seller outreach. 
 We do not run paid advertising. We work alongside an established media, editorial and community program (including the eCom Logistics Podcast and the CrossDock community), with in-house design support and a RevOps lead who owns HubSpot configuration and funnel reporting. We use AI extensively for research, drafting, repurposing and analysis, with human verification and clear accountability for every published claim. 
 The Role 
 You will own the content that has to produce pipeline: offer pages, case studies, executive posts, email and seller material for supply chain, logistics and 3PL buyers. This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who already knows this industry, writes with authority, and can show what they personally published, improved and measured. 
 You will turn FIQ's practice expertise into content that buyers find, trust and act on. You own discoverability (SEO, GEO, AEO) and distribution, not just publication, and you are measured on whether the content reaches the right people and helps turn them into qualified conversations. You will build on established positioning and offers, not start from scratch, and you will protect factual accuracy as fiercely as you protect the brand voice.
 What You Will Own 
 Buyer-facing content and product marketing 
 Turn established positioning and practice offers into clear buyer messages, offer pages, case studies, sales decks, objection handling and competitive guidance. 
 Interview practice leaders and customers to extract real evidence and original perspective; maintain an approved claims register and never publish a claim that has not been verified and approved. 
 Write thought leadership that demonstrates expertise through specifics, examples and source-backed reasoning. 
 Keep voice and accuracy consistent across the website, LinkedIn, email, case studies and sales material. 
 Discoverability: SEO, GEO and AEO 
 Research buyer questions, search intent and existing coverage; prioritize page improvements and topic development that reach buyers, not just traffic. 
 Own descriptive titles and headings, answer structure, internal linking, accessible text, metadata and CMS publishing. 
 Make content reliable and understandable to people and to search and answer systems through source quality, expert attribution and clear explanation. 
 Diagnose discoverability issues and brief technical support on crawl, indexing, redirects, performance or structured data. Measure visibility honestly; no promised rankings or citations. 
 Distribution and campaign production 
 Create channel-specific LinkedIn posts, email copy and seller follow-up from every priority asset, and assign a distribution plan before anything is published. 
 Produce the content for conference campaigns and named-account campaigns with the Senior Marketing Manager and the Field Marketing Manager: invitations, landing pages, expert-session material and follow-up assets. 
 Repurpose approved podcast and community material with the Community & Media Lead, preserving meaning and permissions. Brief designers on the creative each piece needs. 
 Measurement and editorial operations 
 Track search visibility, qualified visits, inquiries, seller usage and content-assisted conversion; distinguish activity from commercial intent. 
 Run a clear brief, SME review, approval and refresh workflow, with versioned approved assets in SharePoint. 
 Use AI to accelerate research and production; verify sources and edit personally before anything goes out. 
 What Success Looks Like

 Days 1 to 30: audit approved positioning, assets, search performance and distribution; agree the priority buyer questions and the claims-review process. 
 Days 31 to 60: deliver two priority offer kits (page copy, proof, distribution assets and seller follow-up); repair the highest-impact content and tracking gaps. 
 Days 61 to 90: review search, distribution and buyer response; refresh underperforming assets; establish a repeatable expert-to-publication workflow. 
 Year one measures 
 One substantial buyer asset per month and one approved customer story per quarter, subject to expert and customer access. 
 100% of material factual claims supported and approved before publication; every priority asset has an audience, intent, call to action and distribution plan. 
 At least 90% of agreed delivery dates met. 
 Growth in non-brand search visibility and qualified visits, and inquiries from content that Sales accepts as qualified. AI-answer visibility is tracked as a diagnostic, not a quota. 
 What You Bring

 Typically five to eight years in B2B content, technical writing or content and product marketing, with a portfolio that demonstrates personal authorship and editorial judgment.

 Demonstrated distribution through company and executive LinkedIn, email, seller use and relevant communities, with outcomes beyond impressions. 
 Ability to interview subject-matter experts, refine established positioning and make complex services understandable without inventing claims. 
 CMS publishing and search and analytics fluency; able to diagnose content issues and brief technical support on crawl, indexing and site requirements. 
 Rigorous fact-checking, customer permissions and AI editing. Consistent brand narrative and tone across channels. 
 Reliable ownership of briefs, reviews, deadlines and asset maintenance in a small, fast-moving team. 
 Paid-advertising expertise is not required. Demonstrable ownership and execution matter more than any specific title.
 Why You'll Love Working Here

About Us: 
 At Reusables, we’re driven by a vision of a waste-free world and recognize the urgent need to address the environmental impact of our current systems and habits. We believe that meaningful change requires institutions to offer frictionless systems that make sustainability effortless and tangible. 
 What began as a grassroots initiative offering reusable takeout containers to restaurants and cafes in Vancouver, has since grown into an enterprise technology platform reaching institutions across North America. Today, Reusables is helping to eliminate thousands of tonnes of single-use waste each year, empowering businesses to join the journey toward a cleaner, more sustainable future. 
 As a venture-backed and mission-driven company, we are passionate about making impact at scale. We are a young, weirdly talented group of ‘high-octane’ individuals that are relentlessly focused on the planet, people, and profit – in that order. 
 About the Role: 
 You'll own everything outside our door: getting the right parts to our floor at the right cost and time, and getting finished units across borders and onto campuses. That covers sourcing and procurement from suppliers in North America and Asia, inbound and outbound logistics, customs and tariffs. 
 You'll be our first dedicated supply chain hire, so you’ll get to design the end-to-end supply chain that best fits our products and demand cycles, and watch it become a core part of how Reusables runs. Very little of what we do has been done before, so most of what you set up will be one of a kind. Until our Production Manager starts, you'll also cover inventory planning and make sure the floor has what it needs. This is a full-time, permanent position to start in January 2027. 
 Our hardware is designed, built, tested and shipped by a small team in Vancouver, and you’ll report to our Hardware Lead. Most units ship in a summer peak, ahead of each autumn semester. 
 We’re moving from build-to-order to levelled production. From February we build steadily towards the September peak, and servicing and refurbishing units already in the field runs alongside new builds. 
 What You’ll Be Doing: 
 Buy components and purchased units, from electronic and mechanical parts to tablets, displays and enclosures, at the right cost and lead time 
 Be the main contact for our suppliers: negotiate price, MOQs and lead times, track delivery performance and resolve quality issues 
 Own supplier, cost, lead time and MOQ for every part, and bring lower-cost or more available substitutes to engineering for approval 
 Find single-source and long-lead parts, and qualify second sources before they become shortages 
 Turn the production plan and sales pipeline into a forecast, and set reorder points 
 Order ahead of factory shutdowns such as Chinese New Year 
 Arrange inbound freight and outbound shipments to customers in Canada and the US: carriers, rates, tracking and delivery dates 
 Handle HTS classification, country of origin, CUSMA documentation, duties and tariff exposure, working with our customs broker 
 Design and source packaging that protects the product and keeps freight costs down 
 Set the packing specs our production floor follows 
 Set up the inventory and BOM data and tools we need as we grow 
 Report on spend, landed cost per unit, supplier on-time delivery and inventory value 
 How Your Year Looks: 
 January to February: Take over the costed BOM and supplier list, and get orders for the build-ahead and summer peak placed before the Chinese New Year shutdown 
 February to May: Keep parts flowing for levelled production, qualify second sources, and cover inventory planning until our Production Manager is in place 
 June to September: Outbound shipping to campuses in Canada and the US, customs clearance, and chasing anything late 
 October to December: Post-season review of landed cost and supplier performance, and next year's forecast and ordering plan 
 What You’ll Bring To The Team: 
 4+ years in procurement or supply chain at a hardware or electronics manufacturer 
 Experience sourcing electronic and mechanical components, including from suppliers in Asia 
 Working knowledge of Canada–US import and export: HTS codes, CUSMA, tariffs and customs brokers 
 Enough technical depth to read a BOM and a drawing and judge whether a substitute part is a real fit 
 Strong spreadsheet skills and experience with an ERP, MRP or inventory system 
 A strong negotiator who follows through on the details 
 Eligible to work in Canada, and able to work on-site in Vancouver 
 A positive, go-getter attitude: you’re excited by a new challenge every day, and you’ll figure out what you don’t know yet 
 Self-motivated and high ownership: give you a problem and you’ll own it through to the end, without waiting to be told how 
 No ego: we’re focused on the mission and check our egos at the door 
 Nice to have 
 Experience building a supply chain function at a startup 
 APICS CPIM or CSCP, or SCMP designation 
 Experience with PCB assembly houses or contract manufacturers 
 Experience planning inventory for seasonal demand 
 If your background doesn’t perfectly align with the qualifications listed, but you’re confident in your ability to excel in this role, we still want to hear from you! At Reusables, we value diverse experiences and unique perspectives, so don’t hesitate to apply if you believe you can make a meaningful impact. We hire for attitude first. Skills can be taught, so we’d rather meet someone who takes on any task with excitement and figures it out, than someone held back by what they’ve done before. 
 We sincerely appreciate the time and effort of all applicants who express interest in joining our team. While we carefully review each application, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Thank you for considering Reusables as your next career opportunity! 
 Compensation & Key Criteria
 Please note: This is an in-office position at our office in Vancouver, BC. 
 Compensation: $90,000-110,000 CAD per year 
 Start date: January 2027 
 Reports to: Hardware Lead 
 Why You’ll Love Working At Reusables: 
 Benefits package (dental, vision, health) 
 Membership to Outdoor Prolink for discounted outdoor gear 
 A small, fun, low-ego team that loves the work we do together and the impact we have 
 A central, spacious and easy-access office in Vancouver with a friendly, sociable atmosphere and plenty of space to focus 
 Annual offsite with the entire Reusables team 
 Work that ships: what you build, buy or plan ends up on campuses where people use it every day 
 Our Values: 
 Strive for excellence 
 Assume you have something to learn from everyone 
 Play bigger 
 Check your ego at the door 
 See the path forward, not the trees in the way 
 Why Join Us: 
 The ocean already contains 165 million tonnes of plastic, and by 2050, plastic waste could outweigh fish. While recycling is often touted as the solution, only 5% of plastic is actually recycled in the U.S. (9% in Canada). Governments and businesses worldwide are banning single-use plastics and committing to zero-waste solutions by 2030. 
 Reusable packaging is the most sustainable alternative, but adoption has been hindered by cost and operational complexity. Reusables removes these barriers, offering a scalable, tech-enabled solution for food businesses and the institutions that serve them.

 At Reusables, we are building products for a diverse world, and we need a diverse team to do that successfully. We strongly encourage applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, ancestry, place of origin, national origin, Indigenous identity, religion, political belief, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, family status, physical or mental disability, or a criminal conviction unrelated to the role.

 Reusables provides an accessible candidate experience. If you need any accommodations or adjustments throughout the interview process and beyond, please let us know, and we will work with you to provide the necessary support and make reasonable accommodations to facilitate your participation.

 Vous rejoindrez une équipe de pilotage responsable du développement, de l’évolution et du soutien de services en ligne destinés à plusieurs clientèles externes (travailleurs, employeurs, représentants, partenaires et fournisseurs de logiciel). Le mandat s’inscrit dans un vaste plan de transformation numérique, dans un environnement complexe qui réunit de nombreux intervenants.
 Responsabilités 
 Recevoir, analyser et concilier les demandes de changement et d’évolution ; préciser les besoins des utilisateurs
 Décrire la situation actuelle, poser un diagnostic et analyser les impacts opérationnels des solutions
 Participer à l’élaboration des processus ; produire la documentation opérationnelle, les guides utilisateurs et les aides contextuelles
 Rédiger et suivre la stratégie d’essais d’acceptation ; produire les plans, devis et cas d’essais
 Réaliser les essais d’acceptation et de mise en production, documenter les écarts et en assurer le suivi
 Valider les environnements d’essais et de formation ; planifier et approuver les conversions
 Approuver les dossiers fonctionnels et jouer le rôle de propriétaire de produit (PO) au besoin
 Soutenir la mise en production, la post-implantation et le rodage ; offrir le soutien de 2e niveau
 Définir les profils d’accès et effectuer des extractions de données
 Suivre les productions informatiques (paramètres, exécutions quotidiennes, productions ad hoc)
 Animer des ateliers, présenter les livrables et contribuer à la gestion du changement

 8 ans ou plus d’expérience en TI, dont au moins 5 ans comme analyste d’affaires spécialisé en essais d’acceptation, au sein d’une unité de pilotage ou d’une équipe utilisateurs

 Expérience dans l’intégration de solutions d’affaires pour au moins 2 clientèles distinctes (ex. : travailleurs et employeurs, citoyens et entreprises)
 3 ans d’expérience en essais d’acceptation dans des environnements central (mainframe) ou infonuagique
 Expérience dans le secteur public québécois
 Profil recherché 
 Autonome, à l’aise pour communiquer et pour bâtir de bonnes relations de travail.

 Contrat de 36 mois à temps plein (35 h/semaine, de jour, heure du Québec)

 Disponibilité dès le début du mandat et pour toute sa durée

In 1931, electrical draftsman Harry Beck looked at London’s Underground map and saw a system that had become too complicated to understand.
 The maps at the time tried to represent the city geographically. Beck realized that wasn’t what riders actually needed. What mattered was how the system connected: which lines went where, where you could transfer, and the simplest way to get from one place to another. So he redrew the network around those relationships instead. His design became the foundation for the modern Tube map and changed how people navigated London.
 Mercury’s Customer Experience organization has its own increasingly complex network.
 As Mercury grows, the right place for support work will keep changing. Some new or complex work may benefit from starting in an incubation team before we know how it should scale. From there, it might move into Core Support, remain specialized, transition to an outsourced partner, or become increasingly supported by AI-powered tooling. The challenge is knowing where work belongs at each stage of its lifecycle, when it’s ready to move, and how to make those transitions without compromising the customer experience.
 For the first 9–12 months, a significant majority of your work will focus on our growing BPO partnership. You’ll identify opportunities to expand the work we deliver through that partnership, build the operational and financial case for doing so, align CX leadership around those recommendations, and lead approved transitions from initial scoping through stabilization.
 Over time, the scope will broaden. You’ll apply the same thinking across our wider service delivery ecosystem, helping us evaluate when work should enter an incubation model, when it is ready to graduate, and whether its next home should be Core Support, a specialized team, an outsourced partner, AI-powered tooling, or another model as our capabilities evolve.
 You won’t be the sole decision-maker on where work lives. Your role is to develop the recommendation: bring together the data, customer impact, operational realities, and tradeoffs; build a compelling case; and help CX leadership reach a well-informed decision. Once a direction is approved, you’ll own the program that turns it into reality.
 This is a role for someone who can move fluidly between strategy and execution. You should be equally energized by building a strong argument for how our service delivery model should evolve and by working through the operational details required to make that change succeed.
 In this role, you will: 
 Lead high-impact programs that evolve how CX delivers support, with the first 9–12 months heavily focused on expanding and optimizing our BPO partnership.
 Identify opportunities to move work to a different service delivery model and build the case for change using customer, operational, and financial data. This could include recommending that emerging or complex work move into incubation, as well as determining when incubated work is mature enough to transition into Core Support, a specialized team, or our BPO partnership.
 Help define what makes work ready to move. Develop clear criteria for when a workflow needs incubation, when it has reached sufficient maturity and stability to graduate, and which delivery model is best positioned to own it next.
 Evaluate where AI-powered tooling could take on, augment, or reshape support work, and partner with the right teams to build a clear case for when automation creates a better customer and business outcome.
 Lead approved service delivery transitions end to end, whether work is moving into incubation, graduating from incubation, transitioning between internal teams, or moving to an outsourced partner. Own the program from initial scoping and business case through readiness, migration, ramp, stabilization, and handoff into long-term operations.
 Partner across Workforce Management, Enablement, QA, Support, and other teams to build transition plans that account for capacity, training, knowledge transfer, quality, tooling, and operational readiness.
 Define success before a transition begins and measure whether the change actually delivered the intended customer, quality, capacity, and cost outcomes.
 Establish clear readiness and stabilization criteria so transitions are judged by whether they work, not simply whether they launched on time.
 Bring structure to complex, ambiguous service delivery questions, identifying the right analysis, stakeholders, dependencies, and tradeoffs required to move from uncertainty to a clear recommendation.
 Build repeatable frameworks and approaches that make future service delivery decisions faster, clearer, and more consistent.
 Use what we learn from each transition to continuously improve how Support evaluates where work should live and how changes should be executed.
 We’re looking for someone who: 
 Has 6+ years of experience in strategic program management, customer experience operations, service delivery, outsourcing, support operations, or a related field.
 Has deep experience with outsourced service delivery and has personally led significant transitions of operational work into a BPO or similar partner environment.
 Understands the operational machinery behind successful BPO transitions, including workforce planning, forecasting, training, knowledge transfer, quality management, ramp planning, and stabilization.
 Can build a strong recommendation without needing to own the final decision. You know how to gather the right evidence, frame tradeoffs clearly, anticipate objections, and create alignment among senior stakeholders.
 Thinks in systems. You naturally look beyond the performance of an individual team to understand how the broader service delivery model works and where changing it could produce a better outcome.
 Is analytically rigorous and commercially minded. You’re comfortable working with operational and financial data, testing assumptions, building business cases, and making recommendations when the answer isn’t obvious.
 Exercises strong judgment in ambiguous environments. You can take a question like “Is this still the right place for this work?” and determine what evidence, tradeoffs, and perspectives are needed to answer it well.
 Can move seamlessly from recommendation to execution. You’re as comfortable developing the case for a service delivery change as you are working through the details required to make it successful.
 Influences effectively without relying on formal authority. You know how to align teams with different priorities and constraints around a shared outcome.
 Communicates complex decisions with clarity. You can explain the customer impact, operational implications, economics, and tradeoffs behind a recommendation without burying the decision in the analysis.
 Holds a high bar for outcomes, not just completion. You care whether a transition delivered what we expected and are willing to revisit assumptions when the data tells us otherwise.
 The ideal candidate may also have: 
 Experience designing or evolving a multi-tier customer support service delivery model.
 Experience with BPO expansions, outsourced operations, vendor launches, or team and site stand-ups.
 Experience moving work between different internal delivery models, such as from incubation to Core Support or between specialized and scaled support teams.
 Experience evaluating how automation and AI-assisted support change the economics, complexity, or appropriate placement of customer support work.
 Experience with incubation or pilot operating models, including determining when new or complex work should be isolated for learning and when it is ready to graduate into a scaled delivery environment.
 Experience using SQL, Google Sheets, or business intelligence tools to evaluate operational performance and build business cases.
 Experience in fintech, financial services, or another regulated environment where risk and operational complexity influence how work can be delivered.

 We are seeking a Senior Automation Manager to design, develop, and implement automation control systems for industrial processes and warehouse distribution equipment. This role requires expertise in engineering principles, programming, and control system technologies, with a focus on maximizing the reliability and performance of conveyors, sortation systems, scanners, cameras, print-and-apply systems, and SCADA devices. The Senior Automation Manager will ensure all work aligns with company policies and procedures, with safety as the highest priority.   
 Serve as site technical expert in automation control systems and lead the site’s automation engineering program.   
 Set program goals, delegate work, and mentor Automation Managers and Apprentices to meet client objectives and safety/technical requirements.   
 Design, develop, implement, and optimize control systems and software; maintain and troubleshoot automation equipment, including PLC/PC controllers and industrial networks.   
 Govern all automation documentation and change management processes for the site.   
 Collaborate with operations, engineering, and support teams to optimize material handling systems and deliver projects.   
 Provide advanced troubleshooting and escalation support, including remote assistance , root cause analysis, and vendor coordination.   
 Monitor system performance, drive continuous improvement projects, and communicate technical issues, timelines, and workarounds to stakeholders.

 2+ years with robotics work cells, control systems, electrical theory, controls components, and automated equipment.   
 Leadership experience in directing, training, and mentoring automation engineers.   
 Proficiency in CMMS use, troubleshooting, and coordinating maintenance with multiple stakeholders.   
 Strong communication skills, policy interpretation, and continuous improvement mindset.   
 Ability to adapt to evolving technologies and build scalable automation solutions.   
 Preferred Qualifications :   
 Advanced degree in relevant field plus 5+ years professional experience.   
 5+ years in PLC programming, troubleshooting, and modification, as well as HMI and control networks, SCADA systems, and motor control systems (VFDs, DC drives, starters).   
 Industrial electrical experience with 480V 3-phase, 110 VAC , 24VDC, and reading/ modifying mechanical and electrical drawings.   
 Proficiency in programming tools such as RSLogix5000 Studio, FT View, and other control software; controls design and systems integration experience.   
 Field service engineering and technical training experience, including conveyors, sortation, ASRS, and industrial robotics.
